reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of this work lies in combining two distinct predictive signals—market-implied spreads and team efficiency metrics—into a coherent ensemble framework. The spread model (M1) leverages historical betting market data, assuming it reflects near-efficient expectations. The efficiency model (M2) incorporates advanced statistical measures such as adjusted offensive and defensive ratings, which are more reflective of underlying team quality. These models are combined using weights optimized on past tournament log-loss, ensuring that the ensemble performs well under the competition's scoring mechanism. The key innovation is the use of log-loss as a loss function, which aligns with the objective of accurate probabilistic forecasting rather than classification accuracy. This approach allows for a principled way to blend different types of information while maintaining theoretical grounding in information theory and statistical learning. The simulation of luck further contextualizes how much of the observed performance can be attributed to skill versus randomness, offering a robust evaluation framework for any predictive system.
